The July reversal saw energy longs drop >30% in a week while financial shorts rallied [D02, D03], demonstrating the peril of adverse factor co-movement in a nominally hedged book [D05]. Liquidity for exit is likely severely constrained [D02, D04].
final.book_exposure: Substantial energy long and financial short exposure [D01, D08], creating sector-relative risk even if dollar net is modest [D02]. Credit and risk arbitrage positions likely add liquidity-sensitive beta [D06].
actions: Reduce energy long exposure to lower factor volatility and collateral call risk [D02, D05]
Trim financial short exposure to manage squeeze risk [D02]
Liquidate lower-liquidity credit and event-driven positions to raise cash and increase portfolio flexibility [D01, D06]
final.target_gross_net: Lower gross and net to de-risk against forced liquidation, aiming to match liquidity with investor withdrawal terms [D02, D06].

drivers.driver: The portfolio faces urgent, joint factor risks in energy and financials that can force liquidations before the underlying thesis is realized [D04, D05].
Thin liquidity and higher collateral calls in a high-volatility regime demand immediate reduction of gross exposure [D02, D04].
July's sharp reversal proved that 'hedged' strategies can suffer simultaneous losses on both sides of the trade [D02, D06].
Counterparty risk and potential redemption pressure make maintaining current leverage levels untenable without a clear liquidity buffer [D01, D06].

final.memo:
The events of July were a warning shot that we ignored at our own peril. We are running an event-driven book, but the environment has transitioned from one of idiosyncratic opportunities to one of systemic liquidity destruction. Our energy longs and financial shorts, which provided a profitable hedge earlier in the year, have turned into a correlated factor trap that is now punishing the portfolio on both sides [D03, D05]. With the VIX near 40, market depth is evaporating, and we must treat our positions as less liquid than the marks suggest [D04].

My priority now is survival to fight another day. We will not be forced sellers in a distressed market because we held onto positions waiting for 'value' to be realized [D05]. We are cutting gross exposure immediately to protect our capital and liquidity, ensuring we can meet potential redemption demands without fire-selling our best assets [D06]. This is not the time to be clever with spreads; it is the time to be ruthless with our risk budget.
